description: Record of real old-release → Squad 2.0 upgrade runs. Produced by test/squad-20-upgrade-matrix.test.ts (SQUAD_UPGRADE_MATRIX=1), merged with `node scripts/render-upgrade-matrix.mjs --merge <results.json>`, rendered into docs/src/content/docs/scenarios/upgrading.md. Producer artifacts are the published ones: npm tarballs through whatever registry npm is configured for (NPM_CONFIG_REGISTRY wins), or the standalone bundle attached to the GitHub Release when that version never reached npm.

producers.why: Oldest 0.x line that still installs on Node 22 (engines >=22.5) and scaffolds .squad/ with a casting registry; predates --state-backend.
Last 0.x stable; first line with --state-backend (local|orphan|two-layer) and personal squads (writes teamRoot when a profile squad exists).
First 1.x stable; last version published to npm (dist-tag latest).
Patch release whose CLI never reached npm (release run 37222633918: SDK publish failed, CLI publish skipped); only the standalone bundles exist.

Latest 1.x release; npm CLI publish failed in release run 39442663504 ("Could not verify @bradygaster/squad-cli@1.1.0 on npm dist-tag 'latest' after 20 attempts"), so the standalone bundle is the only published artifact.
Same-version idempotency: the CLI packed from this tree scaffolds and then upgrades itself.

shapes.default: `squad init` with an empty profile directory, plus a custom agent (`agents/probe/`), an appended decision, a hand-written `.mcp.json` server, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` and a `.gitignore` rule.
shapes.profile: As `default`, but the platform config dir is pre-seeded with a 1.x `squad/personal-squad/` roster and a global `squad/.squad/`; the whole tree must stay sha256-identical and the project must not be linked to it.
shapes.legacy-casting: As `default`, then `.squad/casting/` is replaced by a hand-written `registry.json` (`{universe, agents:[{name, role, status}]}`) with no history — the shape an agent-edited 1.x registry has.
shapes.orphan: `squad init --state-backend orphan` (producers that have the flag); the `squad-state` branch and `stateBackend` must survive.
shapes.two-layer: `squad init --state-backend two-layer` (producers that have the flag); the `squad-state` branch and `stateBackend` must survive.
shapes.ai-team: As `default`, then `.squad/` is renamed to the legacy `.ai-team/` and the upgrade runs with `--migrate-directory`.
shapes.upstream: HEAD only: a second squad is declared via `squad upstream add <path> --name org`; `upstream.json` must survive the upgrade byte-exact.

checks.producer-init: The OLD CLI scaffolds the project non-interactively (exit 0, `.squad/team.md` present).
checks.upgrade-plain: `squad upgrade` (plus `--migrate-directory` for `ai-team`) with the NEW packed CLI exits 0.
checks.coordinator-is-new-template: `.github/agents/squad.agent.md` carries the new version stamp (`<!-- version: X -->`, `Squad (vX)`).
checks.user-state-preserved: `decisions.md`, `agents/probe/charter.md`, `agents/probe/history.md` and `team.md` are byte-identical to the pre-upgrade bytes.
checks.casting-pair-valid: `readCastingRegistryPair` from the packed SDK reads a numbered registry + history; for `legacy-casting` the hand-written original is archived and `probe` is in the repaired registry.
checks.state-backend-preserved: `config.json` `stateBackend` is unchanged; for `orphan`/`two-layer` the `squad-state` branch still exists.
checks.ai-team-migrated: `.ai-team/` is gone and `.squad/team.md` exists (only for the `ai-team` shape).
checks.team-root-absent: `config.json` has no `teamRoot` after the upgrade (Squad 2.0 never links a project to a profile directory).
checks.profile-untouched: The seeded `squad/personal-squad/` + `squad/.squad/` profile tree is sha256-identical after every step (only for `profile`).
checks.idempotent-second-upgrade: A second plain `squad upgrade` changes no file (sha256 of every file outside `.git/`).
checks.downgrade-probe: The OLD CLI's `upgrade --dry-run` against a copy of the upgraded project modifies nothing; its exit code and message are recorded as a note.
checks.clients-projected: `squad upgrade --client all --force` exits 0, `config.json` `clients` lists all 7 hosts, and every host projection exists.
checks.user-config-preserved: After projection the user's `.mcp.json` server, `AGENTS.md`/`CLAUDE.md` paragraphs and `.gitignore` rule are intact (for `upstream`: `upstream.json` is byte-identical).
checks.rollback-byte-exact: `uninstallClients(CLIENT_IDS)` from the packed SDK removes every projection and restores `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.gitignore` and the user's `.mcp.json` server byte-exact; preserved state is still untouched.

findings.title: Stale `teamRoot` written by 0.13.x–1.x `init` survives `squad upgrade`; the upgraded project resolves in remote mode against the removed profile squad
repro: Seed a 1.x profile tree under the platform config dir: `<config>/squad/personal-squad/` and `<config>/squad/.squad/` (APPDATA on Windows, XDG_CONFIG_HOME on Linux).

`squad init` with @bradygaster/squad-cli 0.13.1 or 1.0.0 (npm) or the 1.0.1 / 1.1.0 standalone bundle: it prints `✓ Personal squad detected` and writes `.squad/config.json` → `{ "version": 1, "teamRoot": "<config>\\squad" }`.
Upgrade with the 2.0 CLI packed from this tree: `squad upgrade` (exit 0, no warning about teamRoot).

`cat .squad/config.json` still contains `teamRoot: <config>/squad`; `squad doctor` reports `Mode: remote` and ❌ `routing.md`, `casting/registry.json`, `decisions.md` not found — it is reading `<config>/squad/.squad/`, not the project.
findings.observed: `team-root-absent` fails (`teamRoot=<config-home>/squad`) and `doctor` fails for the `profile` shape on every 0.13.1+ producer. The profile tree itself stays sha256-identical (`profile-untouched` passes), so this is a resolution defect, not a write: Squad 2.0 keeps honouring a link to a directory it no longer supports. Expected: `squad upgrade` drops (or refuses with guidance) a `teamRoot` that points at the platform config dir, and the project resolves in local mode.
findings.resolved: Fixed on squad2-c @ 21ecca77 (PR #2279): `squad upgrade` removes a `teamRoot` that resolves to the platform config dir / `~/.squad` / `SQUAD_HOME` (`isRetiredProfileTeamRoot()` in `@bradygaster/squad-sdk/resolution`) and prints `Removed stale teamRoot pointing to <path>; project state is now local`; `--dry-run` previews it; `resolveSquadPaths` treats such a teamRoot as local mode. Dual-root targets are untouched. Verified by this matrix: `team-root-absent` and `doctor` now pass for every 0.13.1+ producer × `profile` on both OSes (the former pins produced `xpass` before removal).

findings.title: `squad upgrade` never recognizes its own stamped coordinator: every run reports "local customizations" and overwrites `squad.agent.md.local-backup`
repro: `squad init` (any producer, including the 2.0 CLI itself), then `squad upgrade` once — a genuine pre-upgrade coordinator is saved to `.github/agents/squad.agent.md.local-backup`.
Run `squad upgrade` again with nothing changed.

Output again says `⚠️ squad.agent.md has local customizations — backed up to squad.agent.md.local-backup`; the backup is overwritten with the pristine current coordinator, so the user's real pre-upgrade copy is gone. The only file whose sha256 changes between run 1 and run 2 is `.github/agents/squad.agent.md.local-backup`.
findings.observed: `idempotent-second-upgrade` fails with exactly `.github/agents/squad.agent.md.local-backup` for every old producer × shape × platform. On a project initialized by the 2.0 CLI itself the warning is printed on every run too (`Already up to date` + `⚠️ … local customizations`), but the overwritten backup is byte-identical, so the HEAD rows are not pinned. Cause: `writeAgentTemplate` strips `<!-- squad-cli vX -->` before comparing, but `stampVersion` writes `<!-- version: X -->`, `- **Version:** X` and `Squad vX`, so a stamped coordinator never equals the template. Expected: a second `squad upgrade` is a byte-for-byte no-op, prints no customization warning, and never touches an existing `.local-backup`.
findings.resolved: Fixed on squad2-c @ 21ecca77 (PR #2279): `stripAgentStamps()` (`@bradygaster/squad-cli/core/upgrade`) normalizes `<!-- version: X -->`, the `- **Version:**` token, `` `Squad vX` ``, `@bradygaster/squad-cli@X` and the legacy `<!-- squad-cli vX -->` before the customization compare, and an identical `.local-backup` is not rewritten. Verified by this matrix: `idempotent-second-upgrade` now passes for every producer × shape on both OSes.

findings.title: Squad 0.9.1 `squad upgrade --dry-run` is not dry: pointed at a 2.0 project it silently downgrades the coordinator, skills, workflows and templates in place
findings.severity: info (historical producer defect — not fixable in 2.0; recorded for the downgrade story)
findings.layer: none — behavior of the published 0.9.1 CLI
repro: Scaffold with 0.9.1 (`npm install @bradygaster/squad-cli@0.9.1`), upgrade with the 2.0 CLI, copy the project.
In the copy run the 0.9.1 CLI: `squad upgrade --dry-run`.

It exits 0, prints the normal upgrade summary (`Preserves user state: …`) and rewrites ~90 files: `.github/agents/squad.agent.md` (back to 0.9.1), `.copilot/skills/*`, `.github/workflows/squad-*.yml`, `.squad/templates/*`, plus stray `.squad/charter.md`, `.squad/roster.md`, `.squad/history.md` … at the state root.
findings.observed: `downgrade-probe` fails for every 0.9.1 row because the dry-run modified files and printed `Upgrade complete: v1.2.0-preview.1 → v0.9.1`; 0.13.1, 1.0.0, 1.0.1 and 1.1.0 honor `--dry-run` (`Run without --dry-run to apply.`, nothing modified) but their preview lists `overwrite .github/workflows/squad-*.yml` etc. — none of the old CLIs has a newer-version guard, so running any of them for real against a 2.0 project downgrades the Squad-owned files. Guidance for users: never run an older CLI against an upgraded repository; re-run `squad upgrade` with the 2.0 CLI to repair a downgraded coordinator (team state is not touched by the downgrade).
